plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior, since you only pay the second-highest bid if you win. Bidding above value risks negative profit if you win at a high price; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $34 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others bid. If I bid exactly my value ($28), I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid, and I always pay less than my value in that case, guaranteeing non-negative profit. Bidding higher risks overpaying (profit could go negative), and bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid my true value.

This is a second-price auction (Vickrey auction), where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. If I bid higher than my value, I risk winning but paying more than the item is worth to me. If I bid lower, I might lose auctions I could have profitably won. Since I only pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid) when I win, bidding exactly my value of $14 maximizes my expected profit regardless of what others bid.
